_about: Notation sheet and distribution summary added by the study app (supplemental). Symbols marked origin=lecture cite the first lecture page that uses them; tests/unit/notation.test.ts checks each evidence pattern against that page. Distribution rows mirror study-content/FORMULA-REFERENCE.md; supplemental=true marks rows the reference flags with † (not explicitly developed in the lectures).

symbols.name: Population size, sample size
symbols.meaning: $N$ = number of elements in the population; $n$ = number of observations in the sample.

symbols.name: Sample data
symbols.meaning: The observations; $x_i$ is the $i$th measurement.

symbols.name: Summation (capital sigma)
symbols.meaning: Add $x_1+x_2+\cdots+x_n$.

symbols.name: Sample mean
symbols.meaning: Average of the sample: $\bar x=\frac1n\sum x_i$.

symbols.name: Population mean
symbols.meaning: Mean of the whole population; also $E[X]$ for a random variable.
symbols.evidence: population mean/average is denoted by 𝜇

symbols.name: Sample median
symbols.meaning: Middle value of the ordered data (average of the two middle values when $n$ is even). The PDF text extraction shows it as “e𝑥”.

symbols.name: Sample standard deviation, sample variance
symbols.meaning: $s^2=\sum(x_i-\bar x)^2/(n-1)$; $s=\sqrt{s^2}$. Same units as the data (variance: squared units).

symbols.name: Population standard deviation, variance
symbols.meaning: Spread of the whole population (divide by $N$); for a random variable $\sigma^2=V(X)$.

symbols.name: z-score
symbols.meaning: $z=(x-\mu)/\sigma$ or $z_i=(x_i-\bar x)/s$: standard deviations above (+) or below (−) the mean.

symbols.name: Quartiles
symbols.meaning: $Q_2$ = median; $Q_1$, $Q_3$ = medians of the lower and upper halves. **Odd $n$: include the median in both halves** (course convention).

symbols.name: Interquartile range
symbols.meaning: $IQR=Q_3-Q_1$, the spread of the middle 50%.

symbols.name: Whisker endpoints
symbols.meaning: $P_1$ = smallest value that is not an outlier; $P_2$ = largest value that is not an outlier. Not the same as the five-number-summary extremes.
symbols.evidence: 𝑃1 = smallest value that is not an outlier

symbols.name: Inner fences (mild outliers)
symbols.meaning: At or beyond an inner fence (equality counts) → outlier; at or beyond the outer fence $Q_1-3IQR$ / $Q_3+3IQR$ → extreme. Boxplot marks: mild ◦, extreme ∗.
symbols.evidence: mild outlier is indicated by a circle

symbols.name: Sample space
symbols.meaning: The set of all possible outcomes of an experiment.

symbols.name: Probability of event A
symbols.meaning: How likely the outcome falls in $A$; $0\le P(A)\le1$.

symbols.name: Complement
symbols.meaning: Outcomes in $S$ that are not in $A$; $P(A^c)=1-P(A)$.

symbols.name: Union, intersection
symbols.meaning: $A\cup B$: $A$ or $B$ (or both). $A\cap B$: both $A$ and $B$.

symbols.name: Permutations
symbols.meaning: Ordered selections of $k$ from $n$: $n!/(n-k)!$.

symbols.name: Combinations (n choose k)
symbols.meaning: Unordered selections of $k$ from $n$: $n!/(k!(n-k)!)$.

symbols.name: Conditional probability
symbols.meaning: Probability of $B$ given that $A$ occurred: $P(A\cap B)/P(A)$.

symbols.name: Random variable and its value
symbols.meaning: Capital $X$ is the random variable; lowercase $x$ is a particular value it can take.

symbols.name: Probability mass / density function
symbols.meaning: Discrete: $p(x)=P(X=x)$. Continuous: $f(x)$ (the notes also write $p(x)$) is a density; probabilities are areas.

symbols.name: Cumulative distribution function
symbols.meaning: Probability at or below $x$. For integer-valued $X$: $P(a\le X\le b)=F(b)-F(a-1)$.

symbols.name: Expected value
symbols.meaning: Long-run mean of $X$: $\sum x\,p(x)$ or $\int x f(x)\,dx$.

symbols.name: Variance and standard deviation of X
symbols.meaning: $V[X]=E[X^2]-E[X]^2$; $sd[X]=\sqrt{V[X]}$. Lessons also write $V(X)$.

symbols.name: Geometric
symbols.meaning: Number of **trials** up to and including the first success (course convention: $x=1,2,\ldots$).

symbols.name: Binomial
symbols.meaning: Number of successes in $n$ independent trials with success probability $p$.

symbols.name: Negative binomial
symbols.meaning: Number of **trials** up to and including the $r$th success.

symbols.name: Hypergeometric
symbols.meaning: Successes in a sample of $n$ drawn without replacement from $N$ items of which $M$ are successes.

symbols.name: Poisson
symbols.meaning: Count of events in a fixed interval; $\lambda$ = mean count = rate × length.

symbols.name: Continuous uniform
symbols.meaning: Constant density $1/(b-a)$ on $[a,b]$.

symbols.name: Gamma (scale β)
symbols.meaning: Shape $\alpha$, **scale** $\beta$: mean $\alpha\beta$, variance $\alpha\beta^2$.

symbols.name: Exponential (scale β)
symbols.meaning: $\Gamma(1,\beta)$: waiting time to the first event; mean $\beta$ = 1/rate.

symbols.name: Chi-squared
symbols.meaning:
$\Gamma(
u/2,\,2)$; mean $
u$, variance $2
u$.

symbols.name: Normal
symbols.meaning: Second parameter is the **variance**. $N(5,4)$ has standard deviation 2.

symbols.name: Standard normal
symbols.meaning: $Z=(X-\mu)/\sigma$. Probabilities come from the standard normal table (Table V).
symbols.evidence: Table V gives the standard normal cdf

symbols.name: Standard normal CDF
symbols.meaning: $\Phi(z)=P(Z\le z)$. Used in the course-notes synthesis; the lectures refer to “Table V”.

symbols.name: Joint distribution
symbols.meaning: $P(X=x,Y=y)$ (or a joint density). Marginals: sum or integrate out the other variable.

symbols.name: Covariance
symbols.meaning: $E[XY]-E[X]E[Y]$: direction of linear co-movement; units are x-units × y-units.

symbols.name: Population correlation
symbols.meaning: $\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)/(sd[X]\,sd[Y])$, between −1 and 1, unitless.

symbols.name: Sample correlation coefficient
symbols.meaning: Estimates $\rho$ from paired data. Lecture strength guide: |R| ≥ 0.8 strong, 0.5–0.8 moderate, below 0.5 weak.

symbols.name: Least-squares line
symbols.meaning: Slope $b=R\,s_y/s_x$, intercept $a=\bar y-b\bar x$.

symbols.name: Coefficient of determination
symbols.meaning: $R^2\cdot100\%$ = percent of the variation in $y$ explained by the linear fit.

symbols.name: Estimator of θ
symbols.meaning: A statistic used to estimate a parameter $\theta$; $\operatorname{Bias}(\hat\theta)=E[\hat\theta]-\theta$.

symbols.name: Sample mean and variance as random variables
symbols.meaning: Capitals denote statistics before the data are observed; $E[\bar X]=\mu$, $V(\bar X)=\sigma^2/n$.

symbols.name: Standard error
symbols.meaning: Standard deviation of an estimator, e.g. of the sample mean.
